newsitem.title: RUSSIA: NATO's Solana arrives in Moscow for talks.
newsitem.headline: NATO's Solana arrives in Moscow for talks.

text.p: NATO Secretary General Javier Solana arrived in Moscow on Tuesday for talks with Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, who is under orders from President Boris Yeltsin to be tough in negotiations on a planned Russia-NATO deal.

Primakov said earlier on Tuesday that Russia still hoped the sixth round of talks with Solana would be the last before May 27, when Yeltsin hopes to sign an agreement with leaders of the 16 NATO member states at a summit in Paris.
The Russia-NATO deal is intended to overcome Moscow's strong objections to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's plans to expand to take in new members from the former Soviet bloc.

"We would like it to be so (the last meeting), but not everything depends on us. Let us wait and see what Mr Solana brings," Primakov earlier told a news conference with visiting Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti.

Itar-Tass news agency, quoting presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky, said Yeltsin had told Primakov to maintain a firm line, defending the country's interests, particularly on military matters.
Solana, who met Primakov in Luxembourg last week, was expected to keep a low public profile and not to meet reporters in Moscow.
Yeltsin does not plan to meet the NATO chief but may telephone him during his stay in Moscow, Yastrzhembsky said.

The main disagreements over a deal defining a new partnership between the former Cold War foes include Moscow's demands for written guarantees that the alliance will not move its military might into new member states.
